title: Area Manager Salary: How to Calculate Your Annual Pay from Hourly Rates
description: Learn how to calculate an area manager salary from hourly rates, including casual loading, superannuation, and tax. Use our timesheet tool for accurate estimates.
salarySummary: For a full-time area manager working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super and casual loading added on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for an area manager in Australia?
faqs.a: Area manager salaries vary by industry and award. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), which equates to about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. However, many area managers are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set specific rates. Check the relevant pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman or your enterprise agreement for the exact classification.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect an area manager salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $50 per hour, the casual rate becomes $62.50 per hour. Superannuation is paid on the base rate plus loading. Use the casual loading checkbox on [the timesheet](/) to see the difference.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the advertised hourly rate?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of the hourly rate. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Always check if a salary offer includes super or is exclusive. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how to factor it in.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Area Manager Salary

When you're evaluating an area manager salary, it helps to break it down into hourly, weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures. Whether you're negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary gives you a clearer picture of your total compensation.

In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours. The formula for annual gross pay is simple:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time area manager working 38 hours every week, that's hourly × 38 × 52. If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the hours per week accordingly.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the floor for award/agreement-free employees. However, most area managers are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database contains the official minimum rates for each classification, including allowances and penalty rates.

For example, the General Retail Industry Award or the Clerks Award may include a classification for 'Area Manager' or 'Store Manager'. Always check the relevant award on the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) page to find the correct base rate.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you're employed as a casual area manager, you're entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. The casual loading is added to the base rate before calculating superannuation.

**Example:** Base hourly rate $50.00 → Casual rate $62.50 per hour. Super (12%) is then calculated on $62.50, adding $7.50 per hour on top.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% for the 2026–27 year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your annual earnings exceed that cap, your employer does not have to pay super on the excess.

Use the casual loading checkbox on [the timesheet](/) to see how your hourly rate changes when you add the 25% loading.

## Tax on Your Area Manager Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this estimate.

## Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time area manager on $50 per hour:

- Weekly: $50 × 38 = $1,900
- Fortnightly: $1,900 × 2 = $3,800

This can help you budget and compare job offers.

## Area Manager Salary in Context

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, average weekly earnings for full-time adult employees in May 2026 were $2,083.70 (ordinary time). That's about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. An area manager salary often falls near or above this average, depending on industry, experience, and location.

However, many area managers are covered by specific awards that set minimum rates. For example, the Supported Employment Services Award or the Health Professionals and Support Services Award may have classifications that apply. Always verify your classification using the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Commission's database.

## Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, monthly, weekly, and fortnightly figures instantly. Check the casual loading box if you're a casual employee. The tool also estimates super and tax, but remember it's an estimate only. For a precise determination, consult your employer or a tax professional.

## Conclusion

Calculating your area manager salary from an hourly rate is straightforward when you know the formula and the key components: base rate, casual loading, super, and tax. Always refer to official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission for accurate award rates. Use our [reference tables](/data) to compare common classifications, and don't forget that super is paid on top of your hourly rate.

Whether you're negotiating a new role or reviewing your current pay, understanding these elements helps you make informed decisions about your area manager salary.
